theme_strategy.rationale: Food and marine safety monitoring demands authoritative clarity, clean medical/health precision, and accessible high-contrast readability without feeling like a dreary bureaucratic government website. Light mode is warm clean white/slate with deep navy anchors and vibrant status indicators (crimson alert, amber warning, emerald safe, cyan-marine FAO data).

motion.prefers_reduced_motion: Respect system accessibility settings by turning off staggered motion when media query matches.

accessibility.color_independence: All alert severity badges MUST pair distinctive icons and explicit textual labels (e.g. '🔴 Rischio Grave / Microbiologico', '🟡 Attenzione / Allergeni non dichiarati') along with color coding.
accessibility.testing_attributes: All interactive elements (buttons, inputs, filters, tabs, modal triggers, toast triggers) MUST include data-testid attribute in kebab-case.

instructions_to_main_agent: 1. Read this design guidelines carefully. The app is 'Food Alert Italia' — modern, responsive, installable PWA for food & seafood safety monitoring in Italy.
2. Use Outfit for Headings and Plus Jakarta Sans for Body. Import both from @fontsource-variable in frontend/src/index.css.

3. Implement full mobile-first navigation: sticky top header with search & notification count, and fixed bottom navigation bar on mobile viewports (<768px) with Home, Richiami, Dispensa, Mare FAO, and Fonti.

4. In backend/seed.py, seed realistic Italian food alerts (e.g., Listeria in formaggio fresco, Salmonella in salume, Allergeni arachidi in biscotti, Corpo estraneo vetro in passata, Istamina in tranci di tonno pinne gialle) and realistic FAO 37 zones (37.1.1 Golfo del Leone, 37.1.3 Mar Tirreno, 37.2.1 Mar Adriatico, 37.2.2 Mar Ionio, 37.3 Mar Egeo, FAO 27 Atlantico Nord-Orientale, FAO 51 Oceano Indiano).
5. Provide robust search & filter capability: search by product name, brand, lot code, or EAN barcode; filter by risk category (microbiologico, chimico, allergeni, fisico) and time range.

6. Build the 'La Mia Dispensa' feature with localStorage / backend sync allowing users to add barcodes/lotti, receive instant warning if a lot matches any recall in the database, and verify status (OK / Controlla Lotto / Richiamo Attivo).

7. Build the 'Sezione Mare & FAO' with quick lookup (e.g. typing '37.2.1' or selecting fish species like Spigola, Orata, Merluzzo) revealing capture zone, map badge, and marine environmental quality matrices (Acqua, Sedimenti, Biota).
8. Add an Admin / Sync Sources panel showing the sync status of Ministero della Salute, RASFF, and ISPRA/ARPA with a manual 'Sincronizza Ora' trigger that shows immediate toast feedback via Sonner.

9. Ensure every button, input, tab, card, and filter has a descriptive data-testid (e.g. data-testid='global-search-input', data-testid='recall-card-1', data-testid='pantry-add-button', data-testid='fao-zone-select').

10. Make sure all contrast ratios meet WCAG AA standards (minimum 4.5:1 for normal text). Add official disclaimer in footer stating that Food Alert Italia aggregates public open data from official authorities.
